commonPoints: Legs alone should reach eye level; save the center column for when you must (Teds, Breathing Color).
A regular tripod suits most everyday shooting and is easier to carry (Teds, Breathing Color).
A tall tripod helps taller photographers, shooting over crowds or obstacles and on uneven ground (Teds, Breathing Color, DPReview thread).
Extra height usually means extra weight and bulk (Teds, Breathing Color, DPReview thread).
Full leg and column extension reduces sharpness (Breathing Color, The Center Column).

ourGain.point: Legs-only height of a named regular and a named tall tripod side by side: Manfrotto MT055XPRO3 55 in (B&H) vs K&F Concept 90 inch 63.8 in (maker); with 5 to 8 in of head and camera the regular one puts the viewfinder at 60 to 63 in, about 5 to 7 in short of a 6 ft shooter's 67 to 68 in eye level, so the column must come up.

A budget tall tripod is not heavier or longer than a sturdy regular one (K&F 4.46 lb and 21.3 in folded vs Manfrotto 5.5 lb and 24 in); it buys height with four thin 16 to 25 mm sections and pays in stiffness at full extension, as reviewer Julie Powell found. Within one tripod family the long version is heavier and scored 11% lower at the same height (The Center Column).
Who needs which: under about 5 ft 10 in on flat ground, regular; 6 ft and over, or slopes, fences and wind, tall legs used partly extended; fly often, check folded length first.

Named owner experiences for both examples: Barbara and James (verified buyers at B&H Photo) on the Manfrotto, Julie Powell (photographer, own blog) on the K&F at full extension, plus DPReview member casperghst42 on the folded length of his tall tripod on flights.

painPoints.pain: The tripod stops below eye level, so a tall photographer has to bend over
painPoints.details: Tall users find regular and compact legs stop short once the center column is left down.

quotes.text: a travel pod will be shorter requiring you to bend over to look through the VF

painPoints.pain: Raising the center column makes the tripod shake after every shutter press
painPoints.details: A tripod that is steady on its legs gets wobbly once the column is cranked up to reach eye level.

quotes.text: That center post can cause vibration and cost rigidity (especially in a windy environment)

painPoints.pain: A tall tripod is too long folded to fly with
painPoints.details: Owners of long tripods say the collapsed length, not the weight, is what gets in the way on flights (two members in one DPReview thread: casperghst42 on a Gitzo GT3543XLS at about 70 cm folded, calson on an RRS TVC-34L).

quotes.text: basically to long to fly with

painPoints.pain: A tall, sturdy tripod is heavy to carry away from the car
painPoints.details: Thread members with tall studio-class legs say weight is the big problem once you cannot park nearby.

painPoints.pain: On a slope a tripod that reaches eye level on flat ground only gets to waist height
painPoints.details: Downhill legs need extra length to keep the camera at a working height on hills.

quotes.text: Longer legs can be extended down the slope, maintaining a higher working height.
